Interesting... @trustin want to take a stab ?

Whenever a buffer is created in Netty 4, SwappedByteBuf and Unsafe are created.  That contributes about 2/3 of slowdown.  Other contributors are reference counting and `instanceof`s.  Will come up with a solution.

Couldn't we create them lazy?

Going to fix it together with buffer pooling
@spullara, Could you test if #742 fixes the regression?  I think it will still be slightly slower than 3.x, but it should be negligible.

```
java.lang.NullPointerException
    at io.netty.handler.codec.ReplayingDecoder.checkpoint(ReplayingDecoder.java:308)
    at redis.netty4.RedisReplyDecoder.checkpoint(RedisReplyDecoder.java:95)
    at redis.netty4.MultiBulkReply.read(MultiBulkReply.java:47)
    at redis.netty4.MultiBulkReply.<init>(MultiBulkReply.java:39)
```

It looks like ReplayingDecoder now requires newInboundBuffer to be called. Not sure how to do the test now.

I added a check to see if the replaying decoder has an internal buffer before checkpointing and can run the test now. Looks much better:

```
ChannelBuffer: 2076
Old ByteBuf: 3014
New ByteBuf: 2220
```

Fairly small regression I can live with :)
@spullara so sounds like a bug if this cause a NPE.. Right ?
